episodes.200485: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms arrived into West Virginia on the afternoon of May 8th ahead of a cold front. Damaging wind gusts accompanying these storms resulted in downed trees and power lines across several counties in the southwestern portions of the state. In Mingo County, a Mesonet station in the town of Ragland measured a 58 mile per hour gust as strong storms moved through the area. There was also an isolated instance of quarter size hail observed in Logan County. The front slid through late that night and concluded the severe weather threat.
episodes.200488: A few supercell thunderstorms moved eastward from Mississippi across western Central Alabama, producing instances of wind damage and quarter-size hail across Marion, Winston, Fayette, and Greene counties. Meanwhile, a cell cluster moved northeastward from near Andalusia into Pike County, with the main cell producing up to golf ball-size hail near Hamilton Crossroads before dissipating in Barbour County.
episodes.200590: A late season winter storm event from May 4th through the 6th dumped two to three feet of snow across the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. This event was followed by a rain on snow event from May 5th through the 8th in which flooding was experienced across a large section of the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains from areas around Mora, to Las Vegas, to Mineral Hill. A fast warmup in temperatures continued beyond May 8th to May 11th exacerbating the snowmelt in the area, allowing for flood impacts to persist in areas around Mora to Rociada.||Key Word: Snowmelt Flooding.
episodes.200629: Scattered supercells developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the late afternoon and evening hours. Large hail was reported in portions of southern middle Tennessee with a few storms.
episodes.200640: Isolated to scattered strong thunderstorms developed during the afternoon lingering into the early evening hours on May 8th in northern Alabama. Small hail was reported and gusty winds knocked down a tree at a couple of locations.
episodes.200650: A thunderstorm produced localized gale-force wind gusts over Tangier Sound overnight.
episodes.200668: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts and severe hail along the Volusia and northern Brevard County coasts.
episodes.200675: A thunderstorm produced severe hail in Lake County.
episodes.201030: A cluster of storms in La Salle County progressed southeastward through the evening hours. These storms intensified and developed into a well-organized MCS with a maturing bow echo feature as it extended into northeastern Duval and Jim Wells counties. An uptick in radar velocity was noted beginning north of San Diego, TX around 8:45pm CDT, with large wet melting hail enforcing a notable stronger surge of northwesterly winds on the southern edge of the storm over west Alice shortly after 9:00pm CDT.||This southern edge of the MCS became the most destructive bowing segment through the rest of the storm's lifespan, resulting in numerous power and transmission poles snapped, metal building structure collapses, and large trees snapped and uprooted. Widespread wind speeds of 70-90 mph were noted, particularly from Alice to Petronila with a few locations seeing wind gusts as high as 115 mph. While we were unable to access the Petronila area to assess the damage further due to numerous downed power and transmission line, photos and videos shared with us suggest that winds in excess of 100 mph continued through this area as well.||Hundreds of power and transmission poles were snapped between Alice and Petronila. Most were snapped near the base, however a few were found to be snapped 10-15 feet above ground, indicating peak winds of 115 mph. In addition, roof damage was observed, along with several rolled over semi-trucks and campers. Overall, the preliminary path length is 54 miles with a max width of 16 miles.
episodes.201037: A cluster of storms in La Salle County progressed southeastward through the evening hours. These storms intensified and developed into a well-organized MCS with a maturing bow echo feature as it crossed South Texas. While the most destructive portions of the system were inland (particularly Alice to Petronila), marine thunderstorm winds were observed over the southern Coastal Bend as the remnants of the MCS continued eastward out over the Gulf.
episodes.201067: A slow moving cold front and mid-level upper trough of low pressure have allowed for multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms to occur across northern Virginia. A localized one to two and a half inches of rain over Faifax County resulted in flooding.
episodes.201147: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through western and central North Dakota along a cold front. One storm became severe producing 62 mph wind gusts at the Minot Airport in Ward County.
episodes.201246: Steep mid level lapse rates along with sufficient instability and deep layer shear ahead of a cold front brought a couple of rounds of showers and thunderstorms to the region. Large hail and damaging wind gusts were reported. In addition, a tornado moved from Holmes county, FL briefly into Geneva county, AL before lifting.
episodes.201343: Several clusters of thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain and evolved into a larger storm complex as it moved east into the southwestern Piedmont and Sandhills during the evening hours. The storm complex produced a swath of wind damage from Randolph to Moore County, with scattered sub-severe hail reported as well.
episodes.201795: Large trough over the eastern US provided enough forcing and shear to force multiple severe and sub-severe thunderstorms during the evening of May 8th into the early morning hours of May 9th. Instability was sufficient to yield a couple of supercells, one of which produced severe hail near Johnston in Edgefield county.
episodes.202056: A front stalled across south-central GA under SW flow aloft combined with diurnal heating over a moist and unstable airmass produced strong afternoon storms.
episodes.202076: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts around Matagorda Bay.
episodes.202299: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in several large hail and a few damaging wind reports across the region on May 8th.  A high-precipitation supercell thunderstorm developed across the Brush Country/Rio Grande Plains by mid afternoon and held together while crossing through the lower/mid Rio Grande Valley.  The supercell produced very large hail across the Brush Country, then dropped a damaging microburst in North McAllen by early evening.
episodes.202402: A mid to upper level disturbance tracked east across the central and southern Appalachians, coinciding with the peak heating and instability during the afternoon hours. Some storms first developed along the Blue Ridge prior to the convection associated with the upper trough, while storms associated with the trough tracked into the area from the west during the mid to late afternoon. Moderate instability with MUCAPE in the 1000-1500 J/kg, and 0-6km shear was between 35-40 knots, with lapse rate increasing to 7 C/km by the afternoon, so all parameters for severe weather were favorable, and both wind damage and hail were reported.
episodes.202571: A surface low developed in the northwestern Gulf and tracking along the Louisiana coastline on May 9th. As moisture surged northward, multiple storms strengthened to severe limits as the atmosphere destabilized.
episodes.202572: A surface low developed in the northwestern Gulf and tracking along the Louisiana coastline on May 9th. As moisture surged northward, training along the leading edge of an appendant warm front created a setup conducive for training of heavy rainfall. Flash flooding occurred across various portions of New Orleans Metro.
episodes.202799: Scattered showers and storms formed ahead of a cold front during the evening of May 8 across central Virginia. A few storms became severe and produced damaging winds.
episodes.202800: Scattered showers and storms formed ahead of a cold front during the evening of May 8 across central Virginia. These showers and storms produced locally heavy rainfall and flash flooding across portions of central Virginia on the evening of May 8.
episodes.202801: Scattered showers and storms formed ahead of a slow-moving cold front during the early morning hours of May 9. These showers and storms produced gusty winds across the Maryland coastal waters and the James River. Additionally, an isolated storm formed across far southeast Virginia during the afternoon. This storm produced gusty winds as it moved over the Virginia coastal waters.
episodes.202802: Isolated severe storms formed across southeast Virginia on the afternoon of May 9 ahead of a slow-moving cold front. These storms produced damaging winds along with sub-severe hail.
episodes.202820: Isolated thunderstorms formed late in the evening in northwest Georgia. One storm over Bartow county produced large hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter. A few other storms in central Georgia produced some isolated gusty winds with minor impacts.
episodes.202876: An upper low moving over the Midwest plus a surface low helped bring a warm and unstable airmass to the region. Supportive shear with straight line hodographs favored large hail in the storms.
episodes.202957: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the southeast South Carolina coast in the early morning hours. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce strong wind gusts along the coast as well as across the adjacent Atlantic coastal waters.
episodes.203218: A slow-moving upper level low pressure system moved across Northeast Pennsylvania during the day. This feature triggered scattered thunderstorms with locally heavy rainfall that led to isolated flash flooding of roads.
episodes.203245: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted across the Lower Texas Gulf and Laguna Madre waters on two occasions on May 8th:  First, during the mid morning through afternoon, then another smaller window during the early to mid evening nearshore, and around/just after midnight (May 9) offshore. Wind gusts in stronger cells ranged from gale (34 knots) to near storm (48 knots) force.  The discrete nature of the cells likely produced areas of hail, but there were no reports as of this writing.
episodes.203259: Thunderstorms developed over the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.203268: A warm front slowly lifted north across the region during the 6th causing rain and thunderstorms. A low pressure system and associated cold front slowly pushed back across the area on the 7th and stalled into the 9th with a couple rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms.
episodes.203367: A couple of severe thunderstorms moved into York County from western North Carolina during the evening. The storms produced large hail in the eastern part of the county.
episodes.203733: During the second week of May, a nearby deep-layered trough and additional rainfall over saturated soils produced localized flash flooding from May 7th to the 11th.
episodes.204333: River flooding was noted along the Cache and Ouachita Rivers.
episodes.206929: A cold front was tracking southeast towards Kentucky during the early morning hours of Thursday, May 8th. But by the time it got into the state, it began to stall. It remained stalled, with a spot low across western Kentucky, for much of the day. It wasn't until about 0Z that WPC analyzed it starting to sink back southward again, quickly reaching the TN border just a few hours later, where it continued to sink into the overnight.  A upper level low and shortwave were also moving through the state during this time, amplifying the instability and lift in the warm sector - which is where eastern Kentucky was located. Hail seemed to be the most common mode of severe weather, not just in Kentucky but in sourrounding states to our south and east, with several 2 inch stones reported in eastern Kentucky.

Just after 7 PM CDT May 8, 2025, a strong microburst descended |from a hail-producing supercell thunderstorm in North McAllen, near the |city line with Edinburg. Damage, mainly to over 100 large mesquite and|live oak tree limbs, occurred between north Taylor Road and north Ware |Road.  Along and just north of Mile 8 1/2 Road, one unanchored |recreational vehicle (RV) was flipped, with several sections of fence |blown down and small portions of the roof removed.  Along Ware Road, one |industrial business lost its sheet metal roof and garage.||The most notable damage was seen east of Ware Road, mainly between Mile 9 |Road and State Road (SR) 107.  In the El Pacifico neighborhood, one residence had|an unanchored RV turned, flipped, and rolled while the residence and several|more had scattered fence and isolated roof damage. One garage door was |blown in. Between Mile 8 1/2 Road and the Sharyland Water Supply Corporation, |widespread damage was seen in the Eldorado at Thousand Oaks Apartment/Duplex |subdivision, with other damage at a new subdivision immediately north. Much|of these neighborhoods' fencing was blown down, several carport stanchions|were snapped or lifted, and at least three homes had partial roof shingle |lift. Windblown fencing and carport material impacted nearby structures, |shattering windows and damaging stucco siding. Wooden power poles and light |poles were leaning to the east and southeast. A few wood-framed buildings |under construction were partially destroyed, and two more unbraced garages|were blown in. South of SR 107, damage was more isolated - mainly to tree |limbs and some fences, but one automobile repair shop along La Lomita Road|had part of its sheet metal roof lifted off.||In all, several dozen homes and a few businesses had some damage, and hundreds |of large tree limbs were blown down with at least ten uprooted.
